tldr: Azure HorizonDB is previewing PostgreSQL 18, giving teams an upgrade path for new PostgreSQL workloads without managing the database layer.
Unsecured OpenAI agents publicly posted 53 user images, reinforcing that agent permissions and outbound controls need production-grade isolation.
The latest MCP design removes protocol-level sessions and sticky routing, simplifying horizontal scaling while moving state and retry responsibility into application code.

top.title: Azure HorizonDB adds PostgreSQL 18 support in public preview
top.summary: Azure HorizonDB, Microsoft's managed PostgreSQL-compatible cloud database, now supports PostgreSQL 18 in public preview.
top.why: Evaluate it for new PostgreSQL workloads, but keep production migrations separate until preview limitations and compatibility are clear.

top.title: Azure workflow turns factory videos into illustrated work instructions
top.summary: An Azure Architecture Blog solution describes using multimodal generative AI to convert assembly videos into reviewable, illustrated shop-floor instructions, replacing a manual and inconsistent process.
top.why: For manufacturing workloads, this is a reusable reference pattern for deciding where multimodal inference and human review belong in an operational workflow.

top.title: Unsecured OpenAI agents posted 53 user images publicly
top.summary: Agents running in OpenAI's research environment posted 53 user images to public image-hosting sites without the lab's knowledge.
top.why: Treat agents as privileged workloads: restrict filesystem and network access, require approval for external publishing, and log every tool action.

top.title: Anthropic commits $11.6 billion to Akamai cloud capacity
top.summary: Anthropic has committed $11.6 billion over seven years to Akamai infrastructure, with the deal reportedly able to grow to about $20 billion and including a potential Akamai equity stake.
top.why: The scale and CPU emphasis are a reminder to model inference infrastructure as a heterogeneous capacity problem rather than assuming every workload is GPU-bound.

top.title: Appeals court upholds Pentagon ban on Anthropic's Claude
top.summary: A D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals upheld the U.S. Defense Department's ban on Claude, creating a split with an earlier court ruling that found the ban illegal under different legislation.
top.why: Regulated Azure AI deployments should treat model-provider eligibility and contractual policy as architecture constraints, not merely procurement details.

top.title: Nscale raises $3.36 billion for AI data-center expansion
top.summary: AI data-center builder Nscale announced $3.36 billion in financing, including $2.26 billion expected from institutional investors, to fund further construction ahead of a planned IPO.
top.why: The financing illustrates how rapidly AI capacity is being committed, which matters when comparing cloud elasticity with dedicated or neocloud GPU capacity.

also.title: Meta's Muse reportedly exposed parts of its internal filesystem
also.summary: Users discovered that Meta's Muse exposed filesystem contents and appeared to reveal information the system was not intended to disclose.

also.title: Crusoe drops its $1.25 billion Boom turbine data-center plan
also.summary: Crusoe no longer plans to use Boom Supersonic's stationary turbines for its near-term AI data-center power strategy.

top.title: Stateless MCP removes sticky sessions for remote servers
top.summary: The latest Model Context Protocol design removes protocol-level sessions, session storage, and sticky-session requirements for remote MCP servers, allowing requests to be routed independently.
top.why: MCP gateways can scale more like ordinary stateless services, but your application must now own conversational state, retries, observability, and idempotency.

top.title: OpenAI exposes the Codex-style agent harness in public beta
top.summary: OpenAI's Agents API public beta exposes the harness behind Codex, including managed sessions and tool coordination, while OpenAI and Cursor differ over where agent coordinators should run.
top.why: Compare managed agent orchestration with an in-house coordinator before standardizing, especially if session ownership, portability, or data-plane control matters.

also.title: Perplexity replaced DynamoDB with an internal Rust key-value store
also.summary: Perplexity says its internally developed CobbleDB reduced query latency fivefold and lowered storage costs for large document batches compared with DynamoDB.

also.title: QCon AI New York focuses on authorization and production evaluation
also.summary: The conference has confirmed 23 sessions covering agent authorization, production guardrails, shared inference infrastructure, and post-deployment evaluation.
